title: Cisco CCNP Data Center Study Guide
description: CCNP Data Center is the niche-but-lucrative Cisco professional track — DCCOR core plus one concentration across Nexus/NX-OS, ACI, UCS compute, storage networking, and now AI infrastructure. The 2026 story: the AI data-center buildout is inflating demand for exactly these skills, and the brand-new DCAI concentration is the most direct certification path into AI-infrastructure engineering in Cisco's portfolio.
audience: Engineers already touching Nexus, ACI, or UCS at work, and infrastructure people deliberately targeting on-prem/colo data center estates — finance, healthcare, government, service providers, and the AI-infrastructure boom. NOT for cloud-only aspirants: this cert is about physical fabrics, not AWS consoles.
why_get_it: The honest pitch is scarcity economics: fewer postings than CCNP Enterprise or Security, but far less competition, and the shops that need Nexus/ACI/UCS/MDS people pay above market because those people are genuinely hard to find. Typical holder ranges run $130–153K, ACI/VXLAN-EVPN specialists clear $150K, and the AI data-center buildout is actively widening the gap. Every exam earns a standalone Specialist credential, DCCOR doubles as the CCIE Data Center qualifying exam, and the new DCAI concentration (live February 2026) makes this the one Cisco track with a direct, certified lane into AI infrastructure — the hottest sub-market in networking.
when_to_get_it: When your work already includes (or is about to include) Nexus, ACI, or UCS — this track rewards proximity to real gear more than any other CCNP. Solid CCNA-level networking is the floor; ACI and UCS can be learned during prep. The classic warning applies double here: pure route/switch people consistently underestimate the Storage Network domain — 20% of DCCOR is Fibre Channel, zoning, and NPV/NPIV, and it's the single most common fail point. Budget real time for it. The DCCOR core is English-only (as are most concentrations; DCNAUTO is also offered in Japanese) — worth knowing for non-native speakers.
salary_note: Read the numbers carefully: ZipRecruiter shows ~$147.5K average for CCNP-DC-tagged roles, but that figure duplicates its generic data-center-engineer number — treat it as a role proxy, not a cert premium. Independent trackers put typical holders at $130–153K, ACI/VXLAN-EVPN specialists at $150K+, and CCIE Data Center at $142–168K. The AI buildout is actively inflating demand. All third-party estimates.
exam_format: Two proctored exams at Pearson VUE (test center or OnVUE): the English-only DCCOR v1.2 core plus one concentration. Multiple-choice, drag-and-drop, performance-based items; counts and passing scores not published. Results in ~48 hours.

exam_structure.name: Implementing Cisco Data Center AI Infrastructure
exam_structure.note: Brand new (first test Feb 2026) — the forward-looking pick and the most direct certified lane into AI-infrastructure engineering. Also earns the Data Center AI Infrastructure Specialist credential.

exam_structure.name: Automating Cisco Data Center Networking Solutions
exam_structure.note: The two-for-one play: uniquely counts toward BOTH CCNP Data Center and CCNP Automation (renamed from DCAUTO in the Feb 2026 rebrand).

recertification_note: 3-year cycle, 80 CE credits on the unified ledger: DCCOR re-pass = 80 CE, concentrations = 40 each, Cisco U training counts, excess rolls over. The DCNAUTO concentration is the strategic renewal pick — its 40 CE serves this cert while also advancing CCNP Automation.

study_steps.title: Gut-check your storage exposure first
study_steps.description: The single most common DCCOR fail story: strong network engineer, never touched Fibre Channel, lost the Storage Network domain. It's 20% of the exam. If SAN is new to you, front-load it — FC fundamentals, zoning, NPV/NPIV — before the comfortable networking domains, not after.

study_steps.title: Choose the concentration by trajectory
study_steps.description: DCACI for the most job postings (ACI anchors the market); DCAI if AI infrastructure is the goal — it's the most direct certified lane anywhere in Cisco's portfolio and doubles as its own Specialist credential; DCNAUTO for the two-for-one toward CCNP Automation; DCID/DCIT for design and ops lanes. Decide early — lab time compounds.

study_steps.title: Solve the lab problem with simulators, not hardware
study_steps.description: Nobody home-labs an ACI fabric or UCS chassis — accept it and use the real answer: Cisco's free DevNet ACI simulator and NX-OS sandboxes, dCloud's guided labs (free with a Cisco account), and CML Personal ($199/yr) for Nexus 9000v networking domains. CML can't emulate ACI or UCS — the sandboxes are not optional extras here, they're the lab.

study_steps.title: Work DCCOR with the OCG plus blueprint deltas
study_steps.description: The DCCOR Official Cert Guide (2nd Ed.) is the standard text but targets v1.1 — supplement the v1.2 'Automation and AI' domain straight from the blueprint and Cisco U's free AI-for-network-engineers primer. CBT Nuggets is one of the few third-party courses already on v1.2.

study_steps.title: Respect the compute domain
study_steps.description: UCS is 25% and it's conceptually different from anything campus: service profiles abstract server identity from hardware, and the exam expects you to think that way. dCloud's UCS/Intersight demos plus the OCG chapters cover it — don't leave it as the 'I'll skim it' domain.

study_steps.title: Sit DCCOR, bank the Specialist and the CCIE door
study_steps.description: 120 minutes, English only, results in ~48 hours. Passing earns Specialist – Data Center Core and qualifies you for the CCIE Data Center lab. Note for planning: CCIE DC is first in line for the new AI lab module (practice labs Feb 2027, live at Cisco Live US 2027) if the expert tier is in your future.

study_steps.title: Close the concentration while fabric concepts are hot
study_steps.description: 90 minutes, $300. DCACI rewards your simulator hours directly; DCAI's blueprint (AI fundamentals 20%, infrastructure 30%, deployment 30%, operations 20%) leans on the core's AI domain plus GPU-cluster networking concepts. Passing completes the CCNP and banks 40 CE.

study_steps.title: Position for the AI buildout deliberately
study_steps.description: The market moment is real: AI data centers are being built faster than people who can network them exist. DCCOR + DCAI plus a public write-up of your lab work (VXLAN fabric design, GPU-cluster networking notes) is a differentiated profile almost nobody holds yet. This is the rare case where being early to a cert is the whole play.

faq.question: Is CCNP Data Center worth it versus CCNP Enterprise?
faq.answer: Different bets. Enterprise has more postings and broader applicability; Data Center has less competition and higher pay per posting, because Nexus/ACI/UCS people are scarce and the shops that need them (finance, healthcare, government, colos, AI buildouts) pay for scarcity. If your work touches DC gear or you're deliberately targeting that world, this track's ROI runs higher. If you want maximum optionality, Enterprise.

faq.question: What's the DCAI concentration and should I take it?
faq.answer: The newest exam in the track (live February 2026): implementing AI infrastructure in the data center — GPU-cluster networking, deployment, data management, operations. Take it if AI infrastructure is your direction: it's the most direct certified lane into that market anywhere in Cisco's portfolio, and being early is the play. Caveat: official Cisco U training is currently the only substantial prep, so budget accordingly. DCACI remains the highest-job-volume pick.

faq.question: Why does everyone warn about the storage domain?
faq.answer: Because it's 20% of DCCOR and lives in territory route/switch people have never seen: Fibre Channel fabrics, zoning, NPV/NPIV, FCoE. It's the single most common fail story on this exam. If SAN is new to you, study it first and twice — the networking domains will still be comfortable when you come back.

faq.question: How do I lab ACI and UCS without a data center?
faq.answer: You don't own them — nobody does at home. The realistic stack: Cisco's free DevNet ACI simulator (the only zero-cost ACI lab in existence), free dCloud guided labs for UCS/Intersight and Nexus Dashboard, and CML Personal ($199/yr) for the Nexus 9000v networking domains. The simulators aren't the budget option here; they're the only option, and the exam is written accordingly.

faq.question: What's the DCNAUTO two-for-one?
faq.answer: The 300-635 DCNAUTO concentration (renamed from DCAUTO in February 2026) uniquely counts toward BOTH CCNP Data Center and CCNP Automation. If automation is anywhere in your plans, it's the most efficient exam in the Cisco catalog — one $300 sitting advances two professional certs and banks 40 CE.

faq.question: Does DCCOR count toward CCIE Data Center?
faq.answer: Yes — same pattern as every track: DCCOR is the CCIE DC qualifying exam. Planning note if the expert tier calls: CCIE Data Center is first in line for the new AI lab module (practice labs February 2027, live at Cisco Live US 2027), so the lab you'd face is evolving — check the current format before committing to a timeline.
